title: Linear Regression
subtitle: Gradient Descent & Ordinary Least Squares
summary: Fit y = wx + b to labeled 2D data by minimizing Mean Squared Error via gradient descent.

evaluationChart.title: MSE Loss vs. Epoch Convergence
evaluationChart.description: Tracks how Mean Squared Error decays monotonically as gradient descent approaches the global minimum.

advantages: Highly interpretable: weights directly quantify feature impact on the target.
Fast training and O(1) inference time with a convex loss surface (guaranteed global minimum).
Serves as the foundational baseline for regression benchmarks.
limitations: Assumes a strict linear relationship; underfits curved or interactive patterns.
Sensitive to extreme outliers due to squared residual penalties.
Multicollinearity between features can destabilize parameter estimates.

formulas.label: Linear Hypothesis
formulas.description: Predicts continuous target y_hat using slope w and bias intercept b.

formulas.label: Mean Squared Error (Loss)
formulas.description: Average squared vertical residual across all n observations.

formulas.label: Gradient Descent Update
formulas.latex: w \leftarrow w - \alpha \frac{2}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\hat{y}_i - y_i)x_i, \quad b \leftarrow b - \alpha \frac{2}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\hat{y}_i - y_i)
formulas.description: Steps opposite to the gradient scaled by learning rate alpha.

hyperparameters.label: Learning Rate (α)
hyperparameters.description: Step size multiplier for gradient updates.

codeTemplates.fromScratch:
import numpy as np

X = np.array([1.0, 1.8, 2.5, 3.2, 4.1, 5.0, 5.8, 6.7, 7.5, 8.4])
y = np.array([2.1, 2.9, 3.4, 4.5, 4.8, 5.9, 6.2, 7.5, 7.9, 9.1])

def fit_linear_regression(X, y, lr=0.02, epochs=25):
    w, b, n = 0.0, 0.0, len(X)
    for _ in range(epochs):
        err = (w * X + b) - y
        w -= lr * (2 / n) * np.dot(err, X)
        b -= lr * (2 / n) * np.sum(err)
    return w, b

w, b = fit_linear_regression(X, y)
print(f'y = {w:.4f}x + {b:.4f}')
codeTemplates.scikitLearn:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error

X = np.array([1.0, 1.8, 2.5, 3.2, 4.1, 5.0, 5.8, 6.7, 7.5, 8.4]).reshape(-1, 1)
y = np.array([2.1, 2.9, 3.4, 4.5, 4.8, 5.9, 6.2, 7.5, 7.9, 9.1])

model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
print(f'y = {model.coef_[0]:.4f}x + {model.intercept_:.4f}')
print(f'MSE: {mean_squared_error(y, model.predict(X)):.4f}')
